questions.stem: A tank barge loaded with dangerous goods is being towed out of a Canadian harbour. What signal does Rule 39 require of her while underway?
options: An all-round red light and flag "B"
Flag "B" only, and not the all-round red light
An all-round red light only
Two all-round red lights in a vertical line
questions.explanation: In Canadian waters of a roadstead, harbour, river, lake or inland waterway, a vessel with dangerous goods shows an all-round red light or flag "B" when not underway, but underway shows flag "B" and not the red light. Two reds in a vertical line mean not under command.

questions.stem: Which vessel does Rule 40 say shall, if practicable, carry a radar reflector or other means of being detected by radar?
options: Only steel vessels over 50 m
A vessel under 20 m, or a vessel built mainly of non-metallic material
Only pleasure craft
Only vessels fitted with their own radar
questions.explanation: Rule 40 applies to a vessel less than 20 m in length or built primarily of non-metallic materials, so that vessels navigating by 3 GHz or 9 GHz radar can detect her. Large steel vessels already give a strong radar echo, and the Rule is not limited to pleasure craft or to vessels with radar.

questions.stem: In which situation does the Rule 40 radar reflector requirement NOT apply to a 9 m fibreglass boat?
options: Crossing a busy shipping lane at night in fog
Working close inshore in daylight, light traffic and good weather, where a reflector is not essential for her safety
Whenever she carries a VHF radio
Whenever she is under sail
questions.explanation: Rule 40 does not apply when the vessel operates in limited traffic, daylight and favourable conditions and compliance is not essential for her safety, or when her small size or operation away from radar navigation makes it impracticable. Fog and a shipping lane at night are exactly when a reflector matters; carrying a VHF or being under sail is not an exception.

questions.stem: A crew member wants to fit a radar beacon (racon-type transponder) to your workboat so ships can see her better. What does Rule 41 say?
options: It is encouraged for all small vessels
No vessel except one in distress may use a transponder sending radar responder or beacon signals in the 3 or 10 cm marine radar bands, apart from authorized exploration or exploitation vessels
It is allowed as long as it is switched off in port
It replaces the need for navigation lights
questions.explanation: Rule 41 bans the use of transponders transmitting radar responder or radar beacon signals in the 3 or 10 cm marine radar bands, except by a vessel in distress or an exploration or exploitation vessel the Minister has authorized. A radar reflector (Rule 40) is the way to improve a small vessel's radar echo.

questions.stem: A drilling vessel is in position with anchors laid 800 m out from her hull. Under Rule 43, how far does her standard safety zone extend, and who may enter?
options: 500 m; any vessel at safe speed
850 m (50 m beyond the anchor pattern); only vessels in distress, saving life, operating for the government with jurisdiction, or with permission from the person in charge
1 mile; nobody under any circumstances
50 m; only supply vessels
questions.explanation: The safety zone runs from the vessel's outer extremities to the greater of 500 m in all directions or 50 m beyond the anchor pattern, here about 850 m. No vessel may navigate in it unless in distress, saving life or assisting, operated for the state with jurisdiction, or given permission by the person in charge. The Minister may set a larger zone.

questions.stem: Under Rule 44, how must a Canadian ODAS that floats with part of its structure above the water be marked and lit, where technically practicable?
options: Red and white vertical stripes with a red ball topmark and a white light flashing every 10 seconds
Coloured yellow, with a yellow X topmark and a yellow light giving five flashes every 20 seconds visible at least 5 miles
Black with two black balls and a white light flashing 50 to 70 times a minute
Orange, with a flag "B" and an all-round red light
questions.explanation: Rule 44 requires a floating ODAS to be yellow, with a shape that cannot be confused with a navigation mark, and where technically practicable a yellow X topmark, a yellow light giving a group of five flashes every 20 seconds visible at least 5 miles, and a sound signal at intervals of not more than two minutes. A Canadian ODAS also shows its identification number. Flag B and the red light are the Rule 39 dangerous goods signals.

questions.stem: Which of these Canadian vessels, all required by Part C to show lights, must be fitted with an alternate system of navigation lights under Rule 46?
options: A 13 m crew boat
An 18 m commercial water taxi
A 25 m cable ferry
A 20 m pleasure yacht
questions.explanation: Rule 46 requires a backup set of masthead lights, sidelights, sternlight and anchor lights on a Canadian vessel required to show lights, but does not apply to vessels under 15 m, cable ferries or pleasure craft. That leaves the 18 m commercial water taxi.

questions.stem: A Coast Guard Auxiliary vessel shows a blue flashing light while searching at the Coast Guard's request. She is crossing ahead of you from port. Which statement is correct?
options: The blue light gives her right of way over all vessels
She may show the blue light as an identification signal, but it does not relieve her from the steering and sailing rules
Auxiliary vessels may never show a blue light
The blue light means she is in distress
questions.explanation: Rule 45 allows government and police vessels in stated situations, and Coast Guard Auxiliary vessels in SAR at Coast Guard request, to show a blue flashing light as an identification signal. It does not relieve them from the Part B steering and sailing rules, so the normal crossing rules still apply.
